question: Which phonemes of the Malini are assigned to the crest, head, eyes, nose, seals, and ears?
premises: The phoneme na is placed on the crest.
The phonemes ṛ, ṝ, ḷ, and ḷḷ are placed on the head-garland.
The phoneme tha is placed on the skull-top, and the upper and lower eyes receive their assigned phonemes.
The phoneme ī is placed on the nose, and ṇu and ṇū are placed on the two seals and two ears.
inference: This verse continues the bodily installation of Malini phonemes by mapping specific syllables to the upper head, eyes, nose, ritual seals, and ears.
uncertainties: The exact parsing of cordhve and dho@nye is compressed in the transmitted text.
The identity of the two mudras or seals is not specified in this verse.
plain_english: Na is placed on the crest; ṛ, ṝ, ḷ, and ḷḷ on the garland of the head; tha on the top of the skull. The upper and lower eyes receive their phonemes, ī is placed on the nose, and ṇu and ṇū on the two seals and the two ears.
